'''Pauline van den Driessche''' (born 1941)<ref name="preface"/> is a British and Canadian [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] who is a [[professor emerita]] in the department of mathematics and statistics at the [[University of Victoria]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.uvic.ca/science/math-statistics/people/adjuncts-emeriti/index.php|title=Adjunct and emeritus professors|publisher=Department of Mathematics and Statistics, University of Victoria|accessdate=2015-09-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910221435/http://www.uvic.ca/science/math-statistics/people/adjuncts-emeriti/index.php|archive-date=10 September 2015|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}.</ref> where she has also held an affiliation in the department of computer science.<ref name="kn"/> Her research interests include [[mathematical biology]], [[matrix analysis]], and [[stability theory]].

==Education and career==
Van den Driessche earned bachelor's and master's degrees in 1961 and 1963 respectively from [[Imperial College London]]. She completed her doctorate in 1964 from the [[Aberystwyth University|University College of Wales]]; her dissertation concerned [[fluid mechanics]].<ref name="preface"/><ref name="kn"/><ref name="iciam"/> She stayed on for a year in Wales as an assistant lecturer;<ref name="preface"/>
she was hired as an assistant professor at the University of Victoria in 1965, and retired in 2006.<ref name="iciam"/>

==Contributions==
In [[mathematical biology]], van den Driessche's contributions include important work on [[delay differential equation]]s and on [[Hopf bifurcation]]s,<ref name="preface"/><ref name="iciam"/> and the effects of changing population size and immigration on [[epidemic]]s.<ref name="kn"/>

She has also done more fundamental research in [[linear algebra]], motivated by applications in mathematical biology.<ref name="kn"/> Her work in this area includes pioneering contributions to the theory of [[combinatorial matrix theory]] in which she proved connections between the sign pattern of a matrix and its stability,<ref name="preface"/><ref name="kn"/><ref name="iciam"/> as well as results on [[matrix decomposition]].<ref name="kn"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 2005, the journal ''[[Linear Algebra and its Applications]]'' published a special issue in her honor.<ref name="preface">{{citation
 | last1 = Kirkland | first1 = S.
 | last2 = McDonald | first2 = J.J.
 | last3 = Olesky | first3 = D.D.
 | last4 = Tsatsomeros | first4 = M.J.
 | date = November 2005
 | doi = 10.1016/j.laa.2005.07.014
 | journal = [[Linear Algebra and Its Applications]]
 | pages = 1–12
 | title = Preface to Special Issue in honor of Pauline van den Driessche
 | volume = 409| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> She was the 2007 winner of the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]],<ref name="kn">{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/Prizes/citations/kn2007.pdf|title=2007 Krieger-Nelson Prize|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|accessdate=2015-09-13}}.</ref> and in the same year became the inaugural [[Olga Taussky-Todd]] Lecturer, an award given every four years at the [[International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] by the [[International Council for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] and [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref name="iciam">{{citation|url=https://iciam.org/olga-taussky-todd-lecture-iciam-2007|title=The Olga Taussky-Todd Lecture at ICIAM 2007|publisher=[[International Council for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|accessdate=2024-04-12}}</ref>
In 2013 she became a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] "for contributions to linear algebra and mathematical biology".<ref>{{citation|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2013|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2013|accessdate=2015-09-09}}.</ref> She received the CAIMS Research Prize from the Canadian Applied and Industrial Mathematics Society in 2019,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://caims.ca/news/caims-research-prize-presented-to-dr-pauline-van-den-driessche/|title=CAIMS Research Prize Presented to Dr. Pauline van den Driessche}}</ref> and the  [[Hans_Schneider_Prize_in_Linear_Algebra|2022 Hans Schneider Prize in Linear Algebra]].
